newsitem.title: RUSSIA: TENNIS-KREMLIN CUP TO GIVE KAFELNIKOV CHANCE TO BOUNCE BACK.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KREMLIN CUP TO GIVE KAFELNIKOV CHANCE TO BOUNCE BACK.

text.p: Yevgeny Kafelnikov gets a chance to bounce back this week from defeat in Sunday's Paris Open final when he starts as top seed on home soil in Moscow's Kremlin Cup.
The French Open champion, the world number three who was beaten 6-2 6-4 7-5 by Sweden's Thomas Enqvist in Paris, faces Russian Davis Cup team mate Andrei Chesnokov in the first round.

Second seed Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia will take on Czech Daniel Vacek, who spoiled the home crowd's fun last year by knocking out local hero Kafelnikov in the semi-final. Germany's Carl-Uwe Steeb went on to win the 1995 event.
Americans Jim Courier and MaliVai Washington are seeded third and sixth respectively in the $820,000 singles event on a Supreme surface at Moscow's Olympic sports centre.
France's Cedric Pioline is fourth seed and Alex Corretja of Spain is fifth. Swiss Marc Rosset is seeded seventh and Spain's Carlos Moya is eighth.
